purpose: One executable lifecycle for cumulative Product custody, reusable campaign-local Platform Agents, checkpoint-bound audits, finalization, scoped holds, Runtime release, and the next-campaign orientation handoff.

holds.rule: A hold pauses only its dependent outcome. The underlying stage, unaffected work, exact resume condition, and authority boundary remain explicit. A hold is never a terminal stage and never changes Product acceptance roots.

transition_journal.rule: Every lifecycle state begins with one content-addressed GENESIS entry and every state mutation, including same-stage custody, hold, evidence, and live-delta updates, appends one event bound to the prior state digest, source stage, target stage, exact event payload, and UTC time. A stage or authority field cannot change by snapshot editing alone; compare-and-swap persists the appended journal with the new state digest.
transition_journal.stage_rule: The last journal target stage must equal the state stage; legal stage transitions are enforced by control/campaign-lifecycle.mjs.

platform_pool.identity_rule: One logical capability identity has one campaign-local execution session and one stable platform worktree. A completed lease may be released and assigned to another Feature Agent in the same campaign; the logical identity and worktree do not change.
platform_pool.supervision_rule: Exactly zero or one Feature Agent holds a supervision lease at a time. Ordinary reports go to the current supervisor. The Campaign Orchestrator schedules availability and prevents collisions but does not become the routine supervisor.
platform_pool.lease_goal_rule: Every request, supervision lease, release receipt, and active writer binds one exact lowercase SHA-256 goal identity. A lease is valid only when its Feature Agent session and role match the current campaign roster.

checkpoint_ledger.rule: Every checkpoint is immutable and binds its parent, commit, tree, worktree, clean/pushed proof, applicable audit plan, reports, reconciliation, and finding disposition. Audits may settle an earlier checkpoint while the first-pass builder advances a later checkpoint.
checkpoint_ledger.terminal_rule: Only the terminal proposed checkpoint must settle every applicable discipline before finalization. Intermediate checkpoints may retain pending or deferred discipline entries.
checkpoint_ledger.repair_rule: An immediate first-pass repair creates a new checkpoint identity on the same logical lineage. A terminal checkpoint is never rewritten in place.

state_binding.rule: Every lifecycle snapshot binds the exact policy epoch and complete acceptance contract used to admit its campaign. A same-campaign transition cannot change either identity without a new admitted campaign state.

runtime_binding.rule: Runtime is one pinned, persistent RUNTIME identity retained across campaigns. The continuity receipt binds its stable identity, environment, capabilities, and retention posture. Deployment evidence must still come from an admitted Runtime/readback adapter.

repository_checkpoint_proof.rule: A checkpoint proof binds one worktree, local and remote identities, clean/pushed flags, observer, time, and observation digest. The controller accepts only the declared readback method; a host/provider adapter must supply the observation rather than a caller merely asserting it.

roster.rule: Every current Orchestrator, Auditor, and Feature Agent identity binds the current campaign ID/version, is active rather than orientation-only, and has a unique session and role. Platform execution sessions cannot collide with roster sessions, and the active writer must resolve to the current Feature Agent or admitted Finalizer custody.

live_closure.rule: ACCEPTED_LIVE_PENDING_CLOSURE requires a content-addressed deployment receipt bound to the exact accepted root, Runtime session, deployed identity, and rollback identity. ACCEPTED_LIVE_CLOSED additionally requires a content-addressed live-audit receipt whose identity is the current independent campaign Auditor (and is not Runtime), plus a closure receipt bound to the same deployed candidate. A nonempty identity string alone is not closure proof.

finalizer.writer_rule: The Feature Agent releases Product custody before the Finalizer receives a fresh exclusive writer lease. The Finalizer completion releases its lease and the campaign root adopts the exact final commit/tree through a recorded FINALIZER_TO_AUDITOR_HANDOFF.
finalizer.goal_rule: Finalizer custody binds the exact correction-goal digest in the Finalizer record and active writer lease.

successor_orientation.rule: Release clearance spawns only the next-campaign Orchestrator in orientation-only custody. No next Auditor, Feature Agent, Platform Agent, or Product writer lease exists before the current campaign reaches accepted-live closure and the next campaign is explicitly admitted. Admission binds one new campaign identity across the successor roster, rejects completed current-campaign sessions, and converts the oriented Orchestrator to active campaign custody. Candidate, live-delta, and final-candidate packets are typed, content-addressed, bound to the current policy and acceptance contract, and validated at the owning transition; an opaque digest cannot satisfy admission.

candidate_contract.rule: PREDEPLOYMENT packets have no parent or live delta. FINAL packets reference the exact predeployment candidate and live delta. Both packet kinds carry source, intent, policy, acceptance, model, and scope references and are validated against the current lifecycle state.

live_delta_contract.rule: A live delta names the exact predeployment candidate and successor campaign identity. Its content-addressed digest is required before final-candidate admission.

acceptance.rule: The Product acceptance engine has exactly three roots. Code quality is an audit discipline only; a material hygiene finding must identify a concrete consequence in one of the three roots or be classified NONBLOCKING_HYGIENE.
acceptance.closure: Deployment clearance requires the executable question-tree proof and compiled Product acceptance receipt. The proof binds the exact question tree, observations, evidence/evaluation identities, derived three-root result, final candidate identity, and independent Auditor attestation; lifecycle validation must call the canonical acceptance bridge rather than accept a parallel digest-shaped state.

heartbeat.rule: The Campaign Orchestrator reconciles liveness, custody, Git, worktree, roster, Runtime, deployment, rollback, and ledger identity every fifteen minutes. A heartbeat does not create an approval queue or pause useful work.
